question:
Two transformations are said to commute if applying the first followed by the second gives the same result as applying the second followed by the first. Consider these four transformations of the coordinate plane:

• a translation \(2\) units to the right,

• a \(90^\circ\) rotation counterclockwise about the origin,

• a reflection across the \(x\)-axis, and

• a dilation centered at the origin with scale factor \(2.\)

Of the \(6\) pairs of distinct transformations from this list, how many commute?
solution:
Write each transformation as a coordinate rule so that we can compare the two possible orders. Let \(T,R,F,D\) denote translation, rotation, reflection, and dilation, respectively. A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation sends a horizontal displacement \(x\) to a vertical displacement \(x\), and a vertical displacement \(y\) to a horizontal displacement \(-y\), so \((x,y)\) maps to \((-y,x)\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
T(x,y)&=(x+2,y),\\
R(x,y)&=(-y,x),\\
F(x,y)&=(x,-y),\\
D(x,y)&=(2x,2y).
\end{aligned}
\]
Two transformations commute only if their compositions agree for every point \((x,y)\). In a composition such as \(T(R(x,y))\), the inner transformation \(R\) is applied first.

Computing both orders for each of the six pairs gives:

| Pair | First composition | Reverse composition | Commute? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| \(T,R\) | \(T(R(x,y))=(-y+2,x)\) | \(R(T(x,y))=(-y,x+2)\) | No |
| \(T,F\) | \(T(F(x,y))=(x+2,-y)\) | \(F(T(x,y))=(x+2,-y)\) | Yes |
| \(T,D\) | \(T(D(x,y))=(2x+2,2y)\) | \(D(T(x,y))=(2x+4,2y)\) | No |
| \(R,F\) | \(R(F(x,y))=(y,x)\) | \(F(R(x,y))=(-y,-x)\) | No |
| \(R,D\) | \(R(D(x,y))=(-2y,2x)\) | \(D(R(x,y))=(-2y,2x)\) | Yes |
| \(F,D\) | \(F(D(x,y))=(2x,-2y)\) | \(D(F(x,y))=(2x,-2y)\) | Yes |

The commuting pairs are \(T,F\), \(R,D\), and \(F,D\). Thus the answer is \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
